summary: Feed s172_triple is degraded: 26.0% duplicates, 34.08 Gbps microbursts (341% of 10 Gbps NDR port), and 93% encrypted bytes exceeds 90% NDR tolerance. Deduplication and load balancing required to restore complete, correct traffic.

findings.root_cause: Traffic from multiple SPAN/TAP sources aggregated without broker deduplication. Same packets seen at two points in network are merged and delivered 2-3x, causing 26% duplicate rate (2883/11093 packets).
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR wastes CPU/storage on duplicates, breaks TCP reassembly, inflates flow counts and anomaly scores, and can hide true detections under noise.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to drop identical packets seen within a short window before delivery, eliminating 26% waste without losing unique traffic.

findings.root_cause: Microbursts peak at 34.08 Gbps in 1ms intervals vs 10 Gbps NDR port capacity (341% overload, 2 overloaded intervals). Single tool port cannot absorb bursts from aggregated feed.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR NIC buffers overflow and drops packets during bursts, creating blind spots where intrusions, C2, and lateral movement are missed.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic flow-aware across multiple 10G NDR ports to absorb 34 Gbps bursts while preserving flow integrity for NDR analysis.

findings.root_cause: 93% of bytes are encrypted (TLS 1.3/QUIC), just above NDR's 90% tolerance. No decryption path configured, so payload is opaque.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR limited to metadata, JA3, and behavioral analysis; cannot inspect payloads for exploits, C2, or exfiltration, reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Add selective out-of-band SSL decryption or key-sharing for allowed categories to restore payload visibility where policy permits, without violating privacy.
